name: Oakhurst United

location.about: A Thames town of about 230,000: barges, breweries and biscuit factories, then the motorway and the tech offices. Six times champions of England - the most of any club between London and the West - and, since the 1980s, one of the big clubs of the modern game.

colours.story: All white since 1875: the club was started by the town cricket club to keep fit in winter, and they played in their cricket whites. The navy trim came in 1891, the year of the first title.

rivals.why: 2018: Oakhurst beat them to the title by a point and in the Charter Cup final - Eastvale have never forgiven it
the South's two big clubs - Kingsmere pipped Oakhurst to the 1969 title on the last day

history.title: The cricketers' club
history.text: Founded in 1875 by the town cricket club, in their whites. Beaten in the Founders' Cup final of 1879, then winners in 1883 (against Northwick), 1887 and 1890 - and champions of England in 1891, with Eastvale second. The Founders' Cup again in 1896.

history.title: Champions again
history.text: Champions in 1901, ahead of Westmoor; the Founders' Cup in 1903 and 1925 (against Darnford). Second to Riverton in 1914 and to Castleford in 1931 - with a season in the Second Division in between, won at the first go in 1923. Champions a third time in 1937, ahead of Castleford.

history.title: Always the bridesmaid
history.text: Second in 1948 and 1949, second again in 1969 - Kingsmere won it on the last day - and beaten in the Founders' Cup finals of 1969 and 1971. A big crowd, a fine side, and nothing to show for it.

history.title: The Thames Valley years
history.text: With the money from the new business parks along the motorway, the best side in the club's history: champions and Charter Cup winners in 1988 (beating Brackenfield in the final), the Charter Cup again in 1994, champions in 1996 - both titles ahead of Whitcombe. Founders' Cup finals lost in 1991 and 1994.

history.title: Down and back to the top
history.text: Relegated in 2004; up through the play-offs in 2005, down again, and back as runners-up in 2007. The Founders' Cup in 2008 (against Castleford) and 2016 (against Northwick), second in 2012 and 2013 - and in 2018 the Double over Eastvale: the title by a point, and the Charter Cup final 2-1.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1891 = 1890-91).

legends.name: Frederick Ashby
legends.note: The cricket club's captain; scored in the 1883 final and lifted the first title.

legends.name: Percy Gamble
legends.note: Two titles, two Founders' Cups - 'the Thames Valley Wizard'.

legends.name: Ken Abbott
legends.note: 702 appearances - the club record; never won a thing, never left.

legends.name: Jim Rourke
legends.note: Two titles, two Charter Cups - the Thames Valley years.

records.attendance: 58,210 v Kingsmere City, League, 1969 (Abbey Meadow, before seating)

badge.about: An oak tree on the river bank, a Thames barge on the water, and six stars for the six titles. Motto 'Robur in Radice' - strength in the root.
badge.design: A white shield with a navy border. A broad navy oak tree fills the top half, its roots reaching down to two wavy navy lines of river; on the river a small navy Thames sailing barge with a claret sail. 'OAKHURST UNITED' above the shield; six small navy stars in an arc over the tree.

ground.name: Abbey Meadow

stands.name: Thames Stand
stands.features: the main stand, right on the river: tunnel, dugouts, boxes with a view of the barges

stands.name: Brewery End
stands.features: the home end - one big single tier in white seats, on the site of the old Simonds-style brewery

stands.name: Lock Stand
stands.features: two tiers with the old abbey ruins and the lock behind it

stands.name: Meadow End
stands.features: away fans and families; old and low - the obvious one to rebuild

ground.surroundings: the Thames and a lock right behind the main stand, the ruins of the medieval abbey, old brewery chimneys, glass offices of the business park along the motorway
ground.atmosphere: big, smart and expectant - the Brewery End sings, the rest wait to be entertained
